applies_why: The text is a judge's ruling on a pressed link and decides it by noting that no text's own words state the contrary rather than by weighing chain against chain by footing.
quote: the verb change is real [L1]/[L2] but neither text's own words state the other reading's contrary.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: The phrase 'chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse' versus the retired stating-verse test: either a judge may treat the link as underdetermined because no single verse states the contrary in its own words, or K-C requires weighing the whole pressed chain by footing despite that absence.
why: The judge uses the absence of a verse whose own words state the contrary as the reason for underdetermined, which is the retired stating-verse test rather than chain-against-chain footing.
